brief.headline: Push toward ₹205/kg (bottom of the fair market band) and ask for 45-day terms in exchange for freeing up ₹639 for us — we have no public numbers on them, so lean on market pricing and line up Huhtamaki or Constantia as a second source.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a price of ₹205/kg, the bottom of the market-fair band.
priceAsk.basis: Market asking price for pharma/ORS sachet laminate runs ₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg, and the verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR (top of fair band)' — so ₹205/kg is the low end of what's reasonable and fair in the open market.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days after receipt to 45 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Shifting to 45-day terms frees up ₹639 in cash for us.

brief.financialLeverage: Silk Polypack publishes no financial statements, so we don't know their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. Our annual spend with them is ₹7,775 — a small account. Because we're flying blind on their strength, we should not squeeze hard; instead, use the market price band to justify a fair target and offer longer payment (45 days, worth ₹639 to us) as a trade. At the same time, quietly qualify Huhtamaki or Constantia as a proven second source so we're not locked in.

evidence.point: Market asking price for this laminate is ₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg, verdict 'MARKET-FAIR (top of fair band)'.
BOPET film import unit value (the base substrate) is ₹171.60/kg.
We spend ₹7,775 a year with Silk Polypack.
Moving to 45-day terms frees up ₹639 in cash for us.
Silk Polypack does not publish financials, so we have no revenue, profit or cash picture.

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already a tiny FDC supplier — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets (revenue ₹2,611.64 Cr, health C 59/100).

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of the global Constantia group, converts pharma blister and sachet laminates in India — strong second-source fit for our ORS sachets (revenue ₹222.04 Cr, health D 31/100).

risks: No public financials means we can't see if they're healthy or struggling — don't push so hard that a weak supplier walks or fails.
We spend only ₹7,775/year with them, so we have almost no volume leverage.
The market band is wide (₹205–305/kg) — if we ask for the bottom, they may point to typical ₹250/kg and refuse to move much.
We currently pay on 30-day terms; asking for 45 days may meet resistance unless we sweeten the deal (volume commitment or longer contract).
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to work toward the ₹205/kg floor of the market band for this laminate and shift to 45-day payment terms — that way we both benefit, and we'd be happy to discuss a longer commitment if the economics work.
